Primary mechanism I am testing first
Rendezvous store asymmetry: a subset of ranks never registers with the TCP/c10d store, so the surviving ranks block in the barrier at the end of init_process_group.

Falsifiable hypothesis
H1: fewer than world_size ranks reach the store. Falsifiable: if a store-key dump at hang time shows exactly world_size entries, H1 is dead and the fault is downstream of rendezvous.

Controlled experiment
Controlled experiment: keep the launcher, image and env fixed; change only instrumentation. (1) Wrap init_process_group with a pre-log of RANK/LOCAL_RANK/WORLD_SIZE/MASTER_ADDR/MASTER_PORT and a post-log; (2) run with TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL and NCCL_DEBUG=INFO,NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,ENV; (3) diff the set of ranks that logged pre vs post. Control arm: the same command with world_size reduced to 2 ranks on one node.

Evidence to collect
MEASURED to collect: count of ranks logging pre-init vs post-init; MASTER_ADDR resolution per node (getent hosts); TCP reachability to MASTER_PORT from every node; py-spy dump of one hung rank showing whether the stack sits in store wait or in ncclCommInitRank.

Confounders and boundary conditions
Confounders: a slow-but-not-stuck rendezvous under high node count can look like a hang. ESTIMATE: c10d store registration for 64 ranks is single-digit seconds on a healthy control plane, so a >120 s stall is not normal slowness — derivation: one short TCP round trip per rank, ~<10 ms each on a LAN, times 64 ranks, plus barrier; it is arithmetic on assumed RTT, not a measurement of your fabric.

Decision and rollback
If H1 holds, the fault is scheduler/launcher side (a rank died at import, was OOM-killed by the cgroup, or got the wrong MASTER_ADDR), not NCCL. Rollback gate: apply one change at a time, keep the last known-good launcher spec pinned by commit, and revert immediately if the change does not clear the hang in a single reproduction — stacking env-var changes destroys attribution. If two consecutive single-variable arms fail to reproduce or clear the hang, stop and escalate with the collected rank logs rather than continuing to guess.
risks: Env-var shotgunning (changing several NCCL variables at once) destroys causal attribution
Disabling RDMA to clear a hang silently ships a large throughput regression if left in place
Diagnosing on a sampled subset of nodes misses a per-node fleet inconsistency

NCCL_DEBUG=INFO with NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,ENV from every rank

Assumptions (state them, and correct me if your environment differs): a decoder-only LLM served behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint on a fixed GPU fleet; 'weight-only quantization' means weights stored at reduced precision with activations and accumulation kept at higher precision; and the business goal is cost per served token at a fixed quality bar, not peak benchmark throughput. Every number below is labelled ESTIMATE (derived by arithmetic from stated inputs) or MEASURED (only after you actually collect it on your hardware). I assert no platform-specific fact I have not derived here.

What makes the comparison fair
Define the comparison as a paired A/B on one axis: identical model checkpoint lineage, identical prompts, identical serving stack version, identical GPU type and count; only the weight precision differs.

Falsifiable hypothesis
H1: at a fixed quality bar, the quantized deployment reduces cost per 1M output tokens by a material margin. Falsifiable: if measured quality drops below the bar, or throughput gain is inside the confidence interval of the baseline, H1 fails.

Controlled experiment
Design: two arms, FP16/BF16 baseline vs weight-only quantized, same commit of the server, same tokenizer, same sampling parameters (fix temperature and seed for the quality arm), same request trace replayed from a captured production log. Randomise arm order across repeats to absorb drift in the shared cluster. At least 3 independent runs per arm.

Evidence to collect
MEASURED per arm: TTFT p50/p95, TPOT p50/p95, output tokens/s at each concurrency level, GPU memory high-water mark, and task quality on a held-out set. Report bootstrap 95% confidence intervals over runs, not a single number.

Confounders and boundary conditions
Confounders: KV-cache size is unchanged by weight-only quantization, so memory savings appear in weights only; ESTIMATE: moving weights from 16-bit to 4-bit cuts the weight footprint to roughly a quarter plus scale/zero-point overhead — derivation is bits-per-parameter arithmetic, not a measurement. Freed memory usually buys more KV cache and therefore concurrency, which is where the real throughput gain comes from; attribute it correctly.

Decision and rollback
Rollback gate: revert if quality on the held-out set falls below the agreed bar, or if p95 TTFT regresses beyond the SLO, even if average throughput improves. Record the serving-stack commit, quantization toolchain version and artifact sha256 with every result, or the comparison cannot be reproduced later.
risks: Reporting throughput gains without holding the quality bar fixed
Attributing capacity-driven gains to kernel speed
Single-run numbers without confidence intervals or a baseline noise floor
Unpinned calibration data making the quantized artifact irreproducible
evidence_required: Replayed production request trace with recorded arrival pattern
Per-slice generative quality scores with bootstrap 95% CIs
Baseline-vs-baseline repeat run establishing the evaluation noise floor
Serving-stack commit, quantization toolchain version and artifact sha256
